ledger.journal.title: Group journal
ledger.trial.title: Trial balance
ledger.recon.title: Bank reconciliation
ledger.goneBody: You are not in this group any more, or the group has been deleted. Ask the owner to add you back and this screen fills up again.
ledger.journal.subtitle: Every entry says where the group's money came from and where it went.
ledger.journal.formIntro: One line says where the money came from, the other where it went. The entry is saved only when the two columns are the same number.
ledger.journal.memoPlaceholder: e.g. the mess bill for September
ledger.journal.inCurrency: Every amount on this form is in {currency}.
ledger.journal.readOnly: You can read the journal. To post an entry, ask the group owner or the treasurer.
ledger.journal.savesWhenBalanced: The two columns agree, so this can be saved.
ledger.journal.saveBlocked: Save stays switched off until the debits and the credits are the same number.
ledger.journal.needDate: Give the day this entry belongs to.
ledger.journal.needMemo: Say what this entry is for.
ledger.journal.needLines: An entry needs at least two lines — one debit and one credit.
ledger.journal.needAmount: Line {n} has no amount. Put it on the debit side or the credit side, more than 0.
ledger.journal.oneSide: Line {n} carries a debit and a credit. A line is on one side only — give the credit its own line.
ledger.journal.tooManyLines: An entry can have at most {n} lines. Split it into two entries.
ledger.journal.emptyBody: Start with the money the group already holds: a debit to the account that holds it, and a credit to the group fund for exactly the same amount. Two lines, and the books begin to prove something.
ledger.journal.fromReconcile: Posted from the bank reconciliation, statement line {key}
ledger.journal.reverseBody: This posts a second entry beside it: every debit becomes a credit and the other way round, so the two together move nothing. {ref} itself stays exactly as it was, and the journal will show both of them.
ledger.journal.reverseDate: Day to post the reversal on
ledger.journal.flagIntro: A flag puts a question on the entry. It changes nothing about it: the entry stays exactly as it was posted, and the answer stays under the question.
ledger.journal.flagPlaceholder: e.g. this is the rent, but it sits in Food & drinks
ledger.journal.flagNeed: Say what looks wrong — a question with no reason is not one.
ledger.journal.clearIntro: Say how it was settled. {ref} keeps both the question and the answer, so the next treasurer can see what was done about it.
ledger.journal.unbalancedNote: An entry has to add up. The two columns below do not, so this one did not come through this form and should be looked at.
ledger.trial.subtitle: Every account in this group's books, and the proof that the two columns agree.
ledger.trial.unbalancedBody: These two columns should be the same number and they are not, so something reached the books without going through the journal. Do not rely on this screen until it is put right, and the journal is where the entry is missing.
ledger.trial.downloaded: The table is in your downloads — the same rows, in the same order.
ledger.trial.caption: Trial balance: every account, the balance on each side, and the two totals
ledger.trial.tableNote: Every account the group has, whether or not anything was ever posted to it. The Balance column is what the account is left holding.
ledger.trial.contextNote: This journal is the group's own money: what is in the bank and where it went. The split board on the group screen asks a different question — who owes whom for the mess bill — and this screen answers only the first one.
ledger.trial.emptyTitle: This group has no accounts yet
ledger.trial.emptyBody: The books open their own list of accounts the first time this page is read. If it is still empty, the group has not been used yet.
ledger.trial.readOnly: You can read the trial balance. Nothing on this screen writes anything.
ledger.recon.subtitle: Put the bank's figure beside the group's books, line by line, and say what the difference is.
ledger.recon.startIntro: Choose the account, the day the statement is dated, the balance it closes at, and the lines it lists. Anything that can be paired on its own is paired as soon as it can be.
ledger.recon.noAssets: This group has no account that holds money yet, so there is nothing here to set against a bank statement.
ledger.recon.pasteLabel: Paste lines, one per row: date, description, amount
ledger.recon.pasteHelp: A statement arrives as a list, not one line at a time. Separate the three columns with a comma, a tab or a semicolon, and put a minus sign in front of money out.
ledger.recon.pasteBad: Row {n} was left out: it needs a date like 2026-09-28, something to say, and an amount that is not zero.
ledger.recon.pasteTooMany: Only the first {n} lines were kept — that is as many as one reconciliation takes.
ledger.recon.oneTitle: Or one line at a time
ledger.recon.oneAmount: Amount — plus for in, minus for out
ledger.recon.oneNeed: A line needs a date, something to say, and an amount that is not zero.
ledger.recon.draftEmpty: No lines yet. A statement always has some, so this cannot start without one.
ledger.recon.draftGap: The balance you typed is {amount} away from that. A closing balance is what is left after everything the statement covers, so a gap is normal — but a gap nobody expected is usually a line that is missing or a figure that is wrong.
ledger.recon.needDate: Give the day the statement is dated.
ledger.recon.needBalance: Give the balance the statement closes at.
ledger.recon.needLines: Add at least one line from the statement.
ledger.recon.matched: Paired {n} of your lines with entries that were already in the books.
ledger.recon.statementCaption: Every line on the statement, and what has been decided about it
ledger.recon.booksCaption: Every entry in the books for this account, and what has been decided about it
ledger.recon.bookedNote: This line was recorded in the books.
ledger.recon.inTransitHelp: A cheque sent, or a transfer the bank has not shown yet. The line is in the books; the money has not arrived.
ledger.recon.noBookLines: Nothing has moved in this account yet.
ledger.recon.noSessionBody: Nothing to reconcile yet. When you have a bank statement, add its lines here and compare them with what the books say.
ledger.recon.ignoreTitle: Why is this not the group's money?
ledger.recon.ignorePlaceholder: e.g. a transfer from a housemate who shares the account
ledger.recon.ignoreNeed: Write the reason down. It is the first thing the next treasurer will read.
ledger.recon.bookTitle: Record the entry for statement line {key}
ledger.recon.bookNote: This posts a real journal entry against {account} dated {date}, so the line stops being a difference. A posted entry is never edited afterwards — it would be reversed instead.
ledger.recon.bookMemoHelp: Left empty, the bank's own wording is used.
ledger.recon.bookOtherHelp: Money in is counted as income and money out as an expense. Leave the first choice and the books use the usual account; pick another only when the money went somewhere else.
ledger.recon.panelTitle: The difference, and what it means
ledger.recon.tUnbooked: On the statement, not yet in the books
ledger.recon.tAdjusted: The books, once those lines are in
ledger.recon.meansAgree: The statement and the books say the same thing about this account, so there is nothing outstanding between them.
ledger.recon.meansOut: The bank and the books are {amount} apart. Record the entries the books are missing, or explain the lines that are not the group's money, and the two will meet.
ledger.recon.counts: {matched} matched · {book} booked · {ignored} left out · {open} undecided · {outstanding} in transit
ledger.recon.closeBlocked: It cannot close yet, and this is why:
ledger.recon.closedOn: This reconciliation is closed. The next one starts from the statement in front of you.
ledger.recon.readOnly: You can read a reconciliation. To start or finish one, ask the group owner or the treasurer.
ledger.toast.reversed: The mirror entry is in, beside the original.
ledger.toast.flagged: Your question is on the entry.
ledger.toast.closed: Closed — the books and the bank now agree.
ledger.recon.pasteNone: There is nothing in the box to add.
